message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the long‑weekend holidays that Canadians celebrated in **2023**.  
(These are the federal holidays that either fell on a Monday/Friday or were observed on an adjacent day, creating a three‑day break.)

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** (Observed) | Jan 2 (Mon) | Dec 31 – Jan 2 |
| **Family Day** (Ontario, BC, etc.) | Feb 20 (Mon) | Feb 18 – Feb 20 |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 (Fri) | Apr 7 – Apr 8 |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 (Mon) | May 20 – May 22 |
| **Canada Day** (Observed) | Jul 3 (Mon) | Jul 1 – Jul 3 |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 (Mon) | Sep 2 – Sep 4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 (Mon) | Oct 7 – Oct 9 |
| **Christmas** | Dec 25 (Mon) | Dec 23 – Dec 25 |
| **Boxing Day** | Dec 26 (Tue) | Dec 24 – Dec 26 |

> **Note:**  
> - Some provinces have additional holidays that also create long weekends (e.g., St. Patricks’ Day in NL, St. John’s Day in PEI, etc.).  
> - Remembrance Day (Nov 11) fell on a Thursday in 2023, so it did *not* create a long weekend under federal rules.  

Feel free to plug these dates straight into your holiday‑planning app!
